Now I have a clear picture. Let me look at the `strbuflen` definition:

```c
#define strbuflen(buf) strnlen(buf, sizeof(buf) - 1)
```

So `strbuflen(line)` where `line` is `char line[128]` will call `strnlen(line, 127)`. If the buffer is not null-terminated (because `gets()` filled all 128 bytes without a newline), `strnlen` will return 127, and then `val = line + 127` points to the last byte of the buffer. This could lead to out-of-bounds reads.

But more importantly, `strchr(line, '=')` on a non-null-terminated buffer will read past the 128-byte buffer, potentially causing a crash or reading into adjacent memory.
